issue: Does the Fourth Amendment permit an officer to open a car door during a traffic stop without reasonable suspicion, or must the officer have reasonable suspicion to do so?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. IV; Pennsylvania v. Mimms; Maryland v. Wilson

sides.position: Officers may open a car door during a traffic stop without reasonable suspicion, under Mimms and Wilson (the Fifth Circuit's version is limited to opening a door after an occupant is ordered out and claims inability to exit).
cases: United States v. Cotton, 721 F.2d 350 (11th Cir. 1983)
United States v. Meredith, 480 F.3d 366 (5th Cir. 2007)

sides.position: Officers may open a car door during a traffic stop only when they also have reasonable suspicion.

quote: Whether an officer can open a car door during a traffic stop based on less than reasonable suspicion is an open question in our circuit. And our sister courts are divided on the question.
cite: United States v. Donte Dowdell, 70 F.4th 134 (3rd Cir. 2023)
